# Getting started

This guide walks through installing Transform Hub, writing a simple Sequence, and running it on a local Hub. By the end you will have deployed and inspected your first Sequence.

## Prerequisites

- **Node.js** 18 or later (Node.js 20 recommended)
- **npm** 9 or later
- A Unix-like environment (Linux, macOS, or WSL)

Docker and Kubernetes adapters are optional for this guide; the Process adapter is used by default.

## Install Transform Hub

Install the Transform Hub CLI and Hub runtime globally:

```bash
npm install -g @scramjet/sth @scramjet/cli
```

Verify the installation:

```bash
sth --help
```

## Start a local Hub

Start a standalone Hub process with default settings:

```bash
sth
```

The Hub listens on `http://localhost:8000` by default. You should see log output indicating the Hub has started and is ready to accept Sequences.

## Write a Sequence

Create a file named `hello-sequence.js`:

```javascript
import { PassThrough } from "stream";

export default class HelloSequence {
  constructor() {
    this.stream = new PassThrough({ objectMode: true });
  }

  run() {
    // Input data arrives on this.input
    this.input.on("data", (data) => {
      const input = data.toString().trim();
      this.stream.write(`Hello, ${input}!\n`);
    });
    return this.stream;
  }
}
```

This Sequence reads input data, transforms each line by prepending `"Hello, "`, and writes the result to its output stream.

## Package the Sequence

Transform Hub expects Sequences in `.tar.gz` format. The `si` CLI tool handles packaging:

```bash
si sequence pack hello-sequence.js -o hello-sequence.tar.gz
```

## Deploy and run

Deploy the Sequence to the local Hub:

```bash
si sequence deploy hello-sequence.tar.gz
```

The command returns an Instance ID. Send data to the Sequence:

```bash
echo "World" | si instance input <INSTANCE_ID>
```

You should see the output `Hello, World!`.

## Inspect the running Instance

List running Instances:

```bash
si instance list
```

View Instance logs:

```bash
si instance log <INSTANCE_ID>
```

Stop the Instance:

```bash
si instance stop <INSTANCE_ID> <timeout>
```
